messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty HIGH — alert fired for edge.loadbalancer.tls.handshake.rate. Impact: ~7% failed handshakes (eu-west). Auto-escalate in 5m. PD: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/P12345 :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged by oncall-mike (2m ago). Autoresponder: will escalate to SRE lead if not mitigated within 5m.

oncall-mike: ack — I'm oncall and taking lead. Starting quick triage: checking target health, recent deploys, cert rotations. @anya-neteng can you confirm if there was any cert churn or LB config change ~15m ago?

anya-neteng: we pushed a small routing config for weight balancing ~18m ago (deploy id: rwd-2026-03-15-88). No cert rotation scheduled. Seeing lots of SNI mismatch logs on a subset of targets (10.12.34.56, 10.12.34.57). Also noticed DNS TTL for edge.example.net was lowered to 30s earlier which might have triggered re-resolve storms.

raj-sre: pulling metrics — TLS handshake error rate spike lines up with that routing push. Target registration shows flapping on eu-west target-group tg-eu-prim. Could be stale config + DNS rapid re-resolves causing half-open handshakes. Collecting logs now.

emily-cs: Customer impact: support queue has ~18 new tickets reporting 502s / connection reset in EU region. A few enterprise customers report intermittent failures in the last 10m. I'm sending a short "investigating" note.

oncall-mike: quick checks: curl against healthy vs affected nodes shows different TLS responses. Example:
```
# healthy node
$ curl -I https://edge.example.net --resolve 'edge.example.net:443:10.12.34.100'
HTTP/2 200
...

# affected node
$ curl -I https://edge.example.net --resolve 'edge.example.net:443:10.12.34.56'
curl: (35) SSL: no alternative certificate subject name matches target host name
```

anya-neteng: yep that's the SNI/cert mismatch. My hunch: some autoscaled nodes booted with an old cert bundle or the cert sync failed during the config push. Options: 1) weight-shift traffic off tg-eu-prim to tg-eu-fallback, 2) drain and reprovision affected instances, 3) trigger on-demand cert sync. Prefer 1+3 for fastest mitigation.

carol-platform: initiating weight shift now — moving 25% traffic off tg-eu-prim to tg-eu-fallback and enabling conservative connection draining. Command run: `platform-cli traffic shift --from tg-eu-prim --to tg-eu-fallback --percent 25 --note "emergency throttle"` :gear:

raj-sre: watching metrics — handshake failures drop from 7% -> 3.1% within 90s after initial 25% shift. Good signal. Still seeing tail errors from legacy nodes. Recommend full drain for 10.12.34.56/57 and on-demand cert sync.

oncall-mike: starting drain on 10.12.34.56/57. Running deregister command:
```
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:tg:eu-west:111:tg-eu-prim --targets Id=i-0abcde12345 --region eu-west-1
```

anya-neteng: planning cert resync: `scripts/cert-sync --force --targets 10.12.34.56,10.12.34.57` then restart edge-proxy on those nodes. Rolling restart will be staged to avoid capacity loss.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: escalated to SRE lead raj-sre (in 3m) due to ongoing degradation.

emily-cs: pushed update to affected customers: short note + ETA ~30m. Also asked PM for incident banner on status.redwood.ai.

carol-platform: increased fallback capacity and applied throttling on handshake retries at the LB layer to reduce retries that were amplifying load. Command: `platform-cli lb tuning set --region eu-west --handshake-retry-limit 2` :white_check_mark:

raj-sre: after drain + cert sync + retry-throttle we see errors down to ~0.4% and customer tickets plateauing. Traces show successful handshakes on reprovisioned nodes. Recommend watching for 20m before closing.

oncall-mike: putting incident into watch mode. Starting 15m watch window. Preparing postmortem notes: root cause candidate = combo of rapid DNS TTL change + routing config push exposing a small set of nodes with stale certs leading to SNI mismatches and handshake storm. Mitigations performed: weight shift, drain + reprovision, cert resync, handshake retry throttling, customer comms.

incident-bot: Incident resolved — error rate back to baseline (0.1%) after rolling drain and cert resync. PD incident P12345 auto-closed. Monitoring for 1hr. :tada:

emily-cs: Thanks team — support will follow up with impacted customers and log a follow-up for credits if needed. I'll attach a customer impact summary to the incident doc.

raj-sre: filing a follow-up action item: add a preflight check to deploys that modify routing weights when DNS TTL < 60s. Also add cert-sync validation during node bootstrap.

oncall-mike: thanks all, nice quick response. Leaving a short timeline in the incident doc and escalating action items to infra backlog. :thumbsup:"
